text:
nick: quick RFC follow-up — want to land a pragmatic playbook for cutting modules by cohesion (not just by repo). thinking phased, low-risk first slice, clear contract gate, and ops runbook. thoughts?
marin: +1. can we define success criteria per slice? e.g., 95th p50 p95 latency preserved, error budget used < 1%, zero data loss.
alex: agree on metrics. also we should map data ownership: which tables/keys move with the module vs stay in central store. that decision drives migration complexity.
diego: suggest this as phases: 1) read-only facade + dual-write opt-in, 2) verify telemetry + canary, 3) cutover read/write, 4) deprecate old endpoints. keeps rollback simple.
nick: yeah, dual-write for a bounded keyspace seems safest. but follow-up: how do we keep reads consistent during dual-write? strong read-after-write needed for sessions.
marin: option A: sticky routing for keys that are migrated. Option B: read-through cache that checks new module then old store (costly). prefer A for session objects.
alex: sticky routing means we need a routing table service or a bounded prefix-based rule. small operational burden but simple semantics.
diego: we already have the request-router feature flags; can we reuse that for sticky key routing?
nick: we can, but need an infra ticket to add topology awareness (which nodes serve which key ranges). estimate ~3 d of infra work.
marin: also need a pre-deploy test harness: synthetic traffic that exercises both codepaths and asserts no client-visible regressions. simple harness: kotlin load job + smoke assertions.
alex: include deterministic replay of recorded traffic for top customers — that's the biggest risk. store replay artifacts in s3; use them in CI canary.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary for module/session-store-slice at 2025-07-11T14:00Z.
diego: ops checklist draft: roll forward window 15m, backout script (single command), migrate-logs to verify no data loss, heatmap of p95 token latency, synthetic user smoke tests.
nick: we should also define contract compatibility rules: read paths must tolerate missing fields; write schema changes must be opt-in via versioned messages.
marin: +1 on versioned messages. also require a migration advisory doc per slice: owners, data model diff, expected downtime (if any), rollback plan, feature flag toggles.
alex: propose we start with a tiny slice: purely read-only model-profile registry exports (append-only). low risk, easy telemetry. success = stable metrics + migration infra validated.
diego: timeline: proposal + owner signoff this week, infra work next week, canary in two weeks, cutover after 1 week of stable canary.
nick: sounds good. assign owners: alex = migration harness & tests, marin = runbook & contracts, diego = infra changes + feature flag plumbing. i'll coordinate with product for customer communication.
marin: sample feature flag config snippet for reference:
```json
{
  "flag": "module_migration_session_store",
  "scope": "prefix:user_session_v2/*",
  "rollout": 0.05,
  "owners": ["diego"]
}
```
alex: include a smoke-check command in the runbook: `./tools/smoke --replay s3://replays/session-migration/ --asserts smoke.yaml`
diego: we'll also add metric windows to alert on: error_rate > 0.5% sustained 5m, p95 latency delta > +30% vs baseline, write-lag > 2s.
sre-bot: alert-config: created alert module_migration_p95_delta for architecture oncall.
nick: decision summary we should put in the RFC follow-up: phased dual-write with sticky routing, deterministic replay for canaries, contract rules + versioning, owners and runbook. aim to demo first slice in 3 weeks.
marin: 👍 will draft the follow-up doc and ping owners.
alex: I'll stub the CI job and upload a first replay blob.
diego: infra PR coming today.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: canary started for session-store-slice @ canary-1. watch #eng-oncall for automated reports.
nick: thanks everyone — small bites, clear rollbacks, telemetry gates. moving this to RFC-owners triage after doc lands.
marin: adding a checklist item: ensure observability has token-level cost breakdown for migrated traffic (we want to measure unit cost delta).
alex: noted. also flag: caching semantics might change; include cache-warm strategy in runbook to avoid cold-thundering.
diego: one more: DB schema change plan — prefer backward compatible adds, no in-place destructive ops. if unavoidable, schedule during maintenance window.
nick: ok that's the guardrails. closing thread for now, update the doc link when ready. :white_check_mark:
